S42.01.note: The Daily briefing template repeats on weekdays at 08:00 (cadence label Weekdays at 8:00 AM), not every day; Every day is a separate Repeat choice.
steps: Open the side panel, click More, then click Shortcuts. The Options page opens on the Shortcuts section.
Scroll to the Schedules section and click New schedule.
Under Start from a template, click Daily briefing. The Name, Instructions, Repeat and Time fields fill in.
Choose a Model if none is chosen, then click Create schedule.
Compare with Expected: a status line reads Created Daily briefing. It runs in the cloud even when this browser is closed, and the new schedule appears in the Schedules list.
S42.01.where: Side panel > More > Shortcuts (opens Options page on Shortcuts) > Schedules > New schedule > Start from a template > Daily briefing > Create schedule

S42.04.note: The code sets the time zone from the Time zone list and falls back to the browser zone; I did not confirm the list row shows it.
steps: Open the side panel, click More, then click Shortcuts.
In the Schedules section click New schedule and pick a name and prompt.
Set Repeat to Every day, type a value in Time, and open the Time zone list to choose a zone.
Click Create schedule.

Compare with Expected: the new schedule is saved with the time and zone you set. The Time zone list defaults to the browser's own zone, so a different choice should show up. I did not confirm that the schedule list row displays the time and zone.
S42.04.where: Side panel > More > Shortcuts > Schedules > New schedule > Repeat, Time and Time zone fields > Create schedule

labels.text: How can I help you today?

S42.10.needs: a signed-in account with a finished scheduled run that produced an answer, and Task completion notifications turned on
S42.10.note: The notification and its click-to-open path only exist when the run returned an answer; I did not trace whether the follow-up reply itself is correct.
steps: Make sure a scheduled task has finished with an answer (for example Daily briefing after its run).
When the Chrome notification Task Completed appears, click it.
The side panel opens the conversation that holds the scheduled answer.
Click the message box that shows How can I help you today? and type a follow-up question about one item in the briefing, then send.
Compare with Expected: the follow-up is sent in that same conversation and gets a reply about the briefing item.
S42.10.where: Chrome notification "Task Completed" > click it > side panel opens the conversation > type in the message box "How can I help you today?" and send

S42.15.needs: a signed-in account with at least one schedule in the list
S42.15.note: The code audit's quoted lines in apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts (10574, 10577) moved and are a selection-context feature, not pause; the real Pause/Resume button is in apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/schedulesSection.ts near line 905, shown on the Options page, not the side panel.
steps: Open the side panel, click More, then click Shortcuts.
In the Schedules list, find a schedule (create one first with S42.01 if none exists).
Click Pause on that schedule row.
Compare with Expected: the status line reads Schedule paused. and the button on that row now reads Resume.
Click Resume and check the status line reads Schedule resumed. and the button reads Pause again.
S42.15.where: Side panel > More > Shortcuts > Schedules > [schedule row] > Pause, then Resume

S42.17.needs: a signed-in account with at least one schedule, and Chrome notifications allowed for the browser
S42.17.note: The code audit's background.ts line 2482 is the notifications-enabled check and 3436 is the publish call; the notification fires only when the toggle is on. I did not confirm that Run now produces a finished run within a test session.
steps: Open the side panel, click More, then click Extension settings. The Options page opens.
Click Options in the left list and check that the Task completion notifications toggle is on.
Go to Shortcuts, find a schedule in the Schedules list and click Run now.
Wait for the run to finish.
Compare with Expected: a Chrome notification titled Task Completed appears, reading the schedule name and answer snippet or Scheduled task "<name>" finished.
S42.17.where: Side panel > More > Extension settings > Options > Task completion notifications (toggle on); then Shortcuts > Schedules > [schedule row] > Run now and wait for the Chrome notification Task Completed
